ud6.5:19.3: Seated to one side, those mendicants said to the Buddha:
ud6.5:20.1: “Sir, several ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers who follow various other religions are residing in Sāvatthī, holding different views, beliefs, and opinions, relying on different views.
ud6.5:21.1: There were some ascetics and brahmins who had this doctrine and view:
ud6.5:21.2: ‘The self and the cosmos are eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’ …
ud6.5:21.3: they are fighting, quarreling, and disputing, continually wounding each other with barbed words:
ud6.5:21.4: ‘Such is Truth, such is not Truth!
ud6.5:21.5: Such is not Truth, such is Truth!’”
ud6.5:22.1: “The wanderers of other religions are blind and sightless.
ud6.5:22.2: They don’t understand what is beneficial or what is not beneficial, nor what is the truth and what is not the truth.
ud6.5:22.3: That’s why they are fighting, quarreling, and disputing, continually wounding each other with barbed words:
ud6.5:22.4: ‘Such is Truth, such is not Truth!
ud6.5:22.5: Such is not Truth, such is Truth!’”
